text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- About 40 people armed with crude weapons including a petrol bomb are areested and two cars impounded by police during a tense by-election in Langata.
- The government may soon a scheme under which civil servants are paid the same and introduce pay according to their output, says personnel management director.
- The chairman of the opposition FORD-Kenya party rules out any alliance with Kenya's ruling party.
- President Daniel arap Moi thanks the Aga Khan for a grant of 4.4 billion shillings to be used to improve health education facilities.
- Hundreds of students in the central province town of Thika are sent home following an outbreak of a mysterious disease.
- Agriculture Minister Darius Mbela says the government has enough food to meet the needs of drought-stricken areas.
- Industrial court is told journalists are among the lowest paid employees in Kenya.
- The Swedish embassy in Nairobi confirms Nairobi Mayor Dick Waweru was involved in unbecoming behaviour while in Sweden last weekend.
- A severe milk shortage attributed to drought is reported in Nairobi and Mombasa. ($1=54 Kenyan shillings)
